newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Horse Racing-HK authorities to charge two in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-HK authorities to charge two in scandal.

text.p: Hong Kong's anti-corruption police said on Tuesday they would charge two people with taking illegal bets in a horse racing scandal in which 37 people have been hauled in for questioning.
A spokeswoman for the Independent Commission Against Corruption said the two, who were not immediately identified, would appear in court later on Tuesday on illegal bookmaking charges.

The charges were the first announced by the ICAC after it sent 220 of its graft-busting officers into action in its biggest ever sting operation against race fixing and illegal bookmaking at the territory's Shatin track on Sunday.
The team netted 18 people on Sunday night and 19 on Monday including five jockeys, two trainers and three staff of the Hong Kong Jockey Club which has a monopoly on the sport in Hong Kong.
The ICAC said earlier on Tuesday 19 of the detainees had been released on bail and 18 were still being questioned.
The commission, which has extensive powers of investigation, has not yet identified any of the detainees.
